To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we find reduced plasma levels of (25R) 26-Hydroxycholestetol and 7α-Hydroxy-3-Oxocholest-4enoic acid and increased cerebrospinal levels of Bile Acid precursors in Multiple Scleroses Patients.
we find that 25-hydrocholesterol is reduced in plasma from RRMS patients and increased in inflammatory CNS disease.

the concentration of cholesterol in CSF is elevated in patients suffering from amyotrophic lateral scleroris and that the concentration of bile acid precursers in CSF is higher in patients suffering from inflammatory CNS disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of biomarkers that may be useful in the diagnosis and treatment of MS and other neurodegenerative diseases.
the identification of sterols that may be involved in the pathogenesis of MS.
the identification of biomarkers that can be exploited in the diagnosis of CNS diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the levels of 25-hC and 26-HC are decreased in plasma of RRMS patients compared to healthy controls, and that the concentration of these sterols in CSF from patients with inflammatory CNS disorders is elevated compared to healthy controls.

the pattern of sterols measured in plasma is unique to RRMS and reflects an altered cholesterol homeostasis in macrophages, while the pattern of sterol in CSF is unique to inflammatory CNS disease and reflects the presence of demyelinated plaques and/or neuronal death.

the pattern of changes of non-esterified plasma cholesterol metabolites in RRMS patients are consistent with a reduced propensity of macrophage to synthesise 24-hydroxycholecystolic acid, which is the precursor of 25-HO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
25-HCs are reduced in RRMS and elevated in inflammatory CNS disease.

we have identified the pattern of non-esterified steroids that is unique to each of the disease groups and that we have shown that the pattern of steroids in plasma and CSF reflects the underlying pathophysiology of the diseases.
25-Hydroxysterols and bile acid precursors are biomarkers of MS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
25-Hydrocholesterol is reduced in the plasma of MS patients.
25-Hydroxysterols and bile acid precursors are biomarkers that can distinguish MS from other inflammatory CNS disease states.
25-Hydroxylated cholesterol metabolites are reduced in the plasma of RRMS patients and elevated in CSF from patients with inflammatory CNS diseases.
